$description: The Cloudflare account picker: which of the accounts this grant reaches should publishing and the assistant run against. A `jx-dialog`, so the platform owns modality, Escape, focus restoration and the backdrop — which is what retired the `sp-dialog-wrapper` this surface used to open by hand, along with the focus trap and the `aria-modal` slot `showDialog` wrapped around it. There is no confirming button: each row commits itself, because a picker whose answer is one of N rows has N answers rather than one. The adapter (`surfaces/cf-account-picker.ts`) hands in rows that are already strings and booleans — nothing here knows what `cf_account_required` is, which call refused, or whether the list came back empty because the grant reaches nothing or because Cloudflare could not be reached.

style.$description: The picker's own look. Four `.cf-account-picker*` rules in `styles/shell.css` become the parts below and one of them does not come with them: `min-width: 320px` was this surface sizing its own box, and `jx-dialog` is what sizes a dialog now — `sm` is `min(90vw, 24rem)`, which is wider than the 320px it asked for. The row shape came from `.prefs-account`, which the lit template BORROWED from Preferences › Accounts; it is copied here rather than shared, because a class in a stylesheet is a thing two surfaces can drift apart on and `preferences-dialog.ts` still draws its own rows from it. Three token repairs travel with them: `--spectrum-font-size-75` and `--spectrum-font-size-50` resolve only inside `<sp-theme>`, and a document mounted in the dialog layer is outside it, so every one of them would silently have taken its hard-coded fallback.

& [part=\"intro\"], & [part=\"empty\"].$description: The lede and the two absences read as the same secondary line, so they are one rule: the sentence over the list and the sentence drawn instead of it are the same voice.

& [part=\"failure\"].$description: A commit the broker refused, said above the list the reader is still looking at. It is not an announcement of the same thing twice: the list survives a refusal, because listing again is not what would fix an account Cloudflare will not accept, so the reason has to sit beside the rows that are still on offer. It is `failure` rather than `error` because every kit field draws a permanent, empty `[part="error"]` of its own, and the kit is light DOM: a rule on that name here would reach any field this dialog ever holds.

& [part=\"fail\"].$description: The one state that offers a verb of its own. Retrying is right for a listing that never landed and wrong for a grant that genuinely reaches nothing, so the button lives in this branch rather than under both.

& [part=\"text\"].$description: `min-width: 0` lets the column shrink below its content, so the name and id reflow inside the row instead of pushing its own button off the end of it; what lets them reflow is their own `overflow-wrap`. Nothing here ellipsizes. Unlike Preferences › Accounts, the row does not wrap its button onto a line of its own: in an `sm` dialog the arithmetic (a 120px basis, the gap and a 105px button against a 236px row) would wrap every row at rest.

& [part=\"name\"].$description: `overflow-wrap: anywhere` because Cloudflare names a new account after the email that opened it (`name@example.com's Account`), and an address has no break opportunity in it.

& [part=\"detail\"].$description: The account id under the name. Two Cloudflare accounts may carry the same name and the id is what is stored, so the row shows both rather than the half a reader would have to guess from. `overflow-wrap: anywhere` because the id is 32 hex digits with no break opportunity: it measured 203px in a 119px column and ran under the row's own button. It reflows rather than ellipsizing, because the id is the half that tells two same-named accounts apart.

children.textContent: Your Cloudflare login reaches more than one account. Publishing and the assistant both run against the one you pick; you can change it in Preferences › Accounts.

empty.textContent: This Cloudflare login reaches no accounts. Create one at dash.cloudflare.com, then try again.
